ImageDescription.value:
Seven-spot ladybird (Coccinella septempunctata) emerging from its pupa.
Note that even the elytra need to be pumped up; At first wrinkled and "open" towards the hind body. Around 10 minutes after emergence began they're closed, five minutes later they're fully stretched (smooth now) and the beetle has wandered off to find a spot for pumping up the wings. During the pumping of the wings also the colouration of the elytra slowly begins to develop. About half a day later the beetle clearly has its characteristic colours - although still visibly fresh.
Location: Hengelo, Overijssel, Netherlands
Keywords: ladybug, lady beetle, 7-spot
See also: P4b species page (or category).

ImageDescription.value:
Photo by: NPS / Erik Oberg USA: Wyoming, Park County Yellowtone NP, WASH N1 UTM: 546402E 4968210N Pitfall Trap, May 17-30 2018

Coccinella septempunctata

Often seen as a gentle figure in children's books, the seven spotted ladybird beetle is a surprising Yellowstone predator. Although originally native to Europe and North Africa, this insect has been intentionally introduced in the Americas several times to control pests. Agriculturalists highly value its appetite for many kinds of crop-eating aphids. As both a larva and adult, the seven spotted ladybird spits up digestive juices onto its aphid prey, starting external digestion them before devouring them entirely. The seven spotted ladybird beetle has expanded its range throughout the Americas including South America, Canada and the Nearctic, becoming one of the most successful organisms in the Western Hemisphere.

ImageDescription.value: I can clearly remember the first harlequin ladybird I saw, around ten years ago. And I remember what happened after that - all the other ladybirds disappeared. We still get a few seven spot ladybirds and the occasional two spot early in the season. I assume they have overwintered as adults, having hidden away to escape the wave of harlequins the previous year. But after a few weeks they go, then it's harlequins all the way down.
